spec.description: Increasing S-shaped curve crossing the y-axis at −1 and the x-axis at 1, approaching y=−3 on the left and y=1 on the right.

answer.short: Sharp minimum at $(1,0)$; $y$-intercept $1$. The horizontal asymptotes are $y=3$ on the left and $y=1$ on the right.
answer.worked: Keep the portion above the $x$-axis unchanged. Reflect the portion below the $x$-axis across the $x$-axis. Thus $(0,-1)$ becomes $(0,1)$ and the left asymptote becomes $y=3$. The graph meets the unchanged right portion at the sharp point $(1,0)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 21(a); answer-book PDF page 3, top-right continuation labelled (a)
spec.description: Reflected negative portion descends from the left asymptote y=3 through (0,1) to the sharp minimum (1,0); the positive right portion is unchanged and approaches y=1.
spec.mathematics: Uses the exact geometric reflection of the native supplied schematic, without inferring a formula.

answer.short: Symmetric about the $y$-axis, with a sharp minimum at $(0,-1)$, zeros at $x=\pm1$ and horizontal asymptote $y=1$ at both ends.
answer.worked: Delete the portion to the left of the $y$-axis. Keep the right-hand portion and reflect a copy across the $y$-axis. The intercept $(1,0)$ gains a reflected intercept $(-1,0)$; $(0,-1)$ remains fixed. Both ends approach $y=1$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 21(b); answer-book PDF page 3, top-right continuation labelled (b)
spec.description: Even graph formed from the supplied right-hand curve, crossing at x=−1 and x=1 and meeting sharply at (0,−1), with asymptote y=1.
spec.mathematics: Native supplied right-hand Bézier segments and their exact reflection across the y-axis.
